name: Zimbabwe
headline: Zimbabwe: +8.3% growth in 2025, 81.4% inflation, debt 38% of GDP
sections: Zimbabwe is a $58.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 95th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +8.3% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $6,470 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.9% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 81.4% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 193.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 9.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 38% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 57% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.1% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +3.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 42% of GDP (2024), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 26% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 63.1 years (2024). Population: 17.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
